column3: NASB reads “Zabbud,” the written form, for “Zaccur” read aloud. “With him” is rendered “with them.”
NASB reads “I sent them,” the form read aloud. The Hebrew has “Iddo his brother”; NASB reads “Iddo and his brothers.” “Servants” is rendered “ministers.”
“A straight journey” is rendered “a safe journey,” and “property” as “possessions.”
“An escort” is rendered “troops,” and “help” as “protect.” “For good” is rendered “favorably disposed.”
“He was entreated by us” is rendered “He listened to our entreaty.”
“Vessels of silver, a hundred of talents” is rendered “silver utensils worth 100 talents”; the meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
“Gleaming fine bronze” is rendered “fine shiny bronze.”
“Leaders of the fathers” is rendered “heads of the fathers' households,” and “rooms” as “chambers.”
“The weight of” is rendered “the weighed out.”
